description: EHR data stored on systems and databases must be encrypted at rest.
remediation: Enable encryption for databases, storage volumes, and hosted EHR repositories.
plain_language_feedback: Stored patient information should stay protected even if a device or storage system is lost or stolen.
technical_feedback: Verify database, disk, and storage encryption settings and retain screenshots or configuration evidence.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.312(a); NIST SP 800-53 SC-28

description: Backups containing EHR or PHI data must be encrypted.
remediation: Enable encryption for backup storage and protect backup access.
plain_language_feedback: Backups should be protected so patient data is not exposed from backup copies.
technical_feedback: Confirm backup platform encryption settings and collect evidence from backup consoles or policies.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.312(a); NIST SP 800-53 CP-9, SC-28

description: A firewall or equivalent network protection must be enabled.
remediation: Enable firewall protection and document approved inbound and outbound rules.
plain_language_feedback: A firewall helps block unsafe network traffic from reaching healthcare systems.
technical_feedback: Verify host or network firewall rulesets, change control records, and security policy enforcement.

description: Endpoint protection must be enabled on systems handling healthcare data.
remediation: Deploy endpoint protection and confirm signature, telemetry, or policy status.
plain_language_feedback: Security software helps stop malware from reaching patient systems and files.
technical_feedback: Verify EDR or antivirus console status, policy assignments, and update health.

description: Role-based access control must be enabled for workforce access.
remediation: Review role assignments and enforce least-privilege access for EHR users.
plain_language_feedback: Staff should only see the records and systems they need for their job.
technical_feedback: Validate role mappings, access groups, and privileged access restrictions.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.312(a); NIST SP 800-53 AC-2, AC-6

description: Workstations used to access PHI must follow security controls.
remediation: Enforce screen lock, approved device settings, patching, and removable media rules.
plain_language_feedback: Devices used by staff should be protected so patient information is not exposed.
technical_feedback: Check workstation hardening, lock settings, device controls, and endpoint compliance reports.

description: Remote access to healthcare systems must be secured.
remediation: Require VPN, MFA, managed devices, or equivalent secure remote access controls.
plain_language_feedback: Remote access should be protected so outsiders cannot easily enter healthcare systems.
technical_feedback: Review VPN, conditional access, remote desktop restrictions, and MFA enforcement.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.312(e); NIST SP 800-53 AC-17

description: Audit logging must be enabled for EHR and related systems.
remediation: Enable audit logging and retain access, modification, and administrative activity records.
plain_language_feedback: The organization should be able to see who accessed or changed important records.
technical_feedback: Verify logging scope, retention, review procedures, and log source coverage.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.312(b); NIST SP 800-53 AU-2, AU-6

description: A security risk assessment must be completed and current.
remediation: Perform and document a current security risk assessment with tracked remediation actions.
plain_language_feedback: The organization should regularly review its security risks and decide what to fix first.
technical_feedback: Maintain a current risk register, assessment records, and remediation ownership tracking.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A); NIST SP 800-53 RA-3

description: Contingency and disaster recovery planning must be documented.
remediation: Document disaster recovery, recovery contacts, system priorities, and downtime continuity steps.
plain_language_feedback: Healthcare organizations should have a clear recovery plan for outages and emergencies.
technical_feedback: Verify recovery documentation, recovery order, system dependencies, and recovery evidence.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.308(a)(7); NIST SP 800-53 CP-2

description: An incident response plan must be documented.
remediation: Create an incident response plan with roles, triage, escalation, containment, and reporting steps.
plain_language_feedback: The organization should know exactly how it will respond to a security incident.
technical_feedback: Document response workflows, owners, escalation paths, evidence handling, and containment steps.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.308(a)(6); NIST SP 800-53 IR-4

description: A responsible security or privacy contact must be assigned.
remediation: Assign and document a security or privacy contact for incident coordination.
plain_language_feedback: Staff should know who to contact when a security or privacy issue happens.
technical_feedback: Maintain a named incident contact, backup contact, and escalation directory.

description: A breach reporting process must be documented.
remediation: Document breach notification decision points, reporting timelines, and responsible roles.
plain_language_feedback: The organization should know how to report and manage a privacy or security breach.
technical_feedback: Define reporting workflow, legal notification requirements, evidence review, and timeline tracking.
reference: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule; PHIPA breach duties; NIST SP 800-53 IR-6

description: A suspicious activity reporting process must be documented.
remediation: Create a simple reporting process for suspicious emails, logins, data access, or device issues.
plain_language_feedback: Staff should know how to quickly report anything suspicious.
technical_feedback: Document reporting channels, ticket flow, alert escalation, and required reporting details.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.308(a)(6); NIST SP 800-53 IR-6

description: Alert review procedures must exist for suspicious activity and monitoring events.
remediation: Document alert triage and review procedures for security monitoring events.
plain_language_feedback: Security alerts should be reviewed so important warning signs are not missed.
technical_feedback: Verify documented alert triage, escalation criteria, assigned reviewers, and response SLAs.
nist_family: AU – Audit and Accountability; SI – System and Information Integrity

description: Post-incident documentation must be maintained.
remediation: Document timelines, findings, evidence, actions taken, and lessons learned after incidents.
plain_language_feedback: After an incident, the organization should write down what happened and what was fixed.
technical_feedback: Maintain incident reports, evidence references, closure notes, and corrective action records.

description: Staff retraining must occur after incidents when needed.
remediation: Provide targeted follow-up training after phishing, privacy, or process failures.
plain_language_feedback: Staff may need extra training after an incident so the same mistake is less likely to happen again.
technical_feedback: Track corrective training assignments, completion evidence, and incident-linked awareness improvements.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.308(a)(5); NIST SP 800-53 AT-2

description: Backups must be tested regularly.
remediation: Perform and document regular restore tests.
plain_language_feedback: A backup is only useful if it can actually be restored.
technical_feedback: Test restoration workflows and preserve test evidence and validation results.

description: Downtime procedures must be documented.
remediation: Document manual and alternative workflows for outages.
plain_language_feedback: Staff should know what to do when systems are down.
technical_feedback: Maintain downtime workflow instructions, communication steps, and recovery transition records.

description: Ransomware recovery steps must be documented.
remediation: Document isolation, recovery, restoration, and validation steps for ransomware events.
plain_language_feedback: The organization should know how it will recover if ransomware affects systems or files.
technical_feedback: Define isolation, restoration order, validation, and post-recovery review procedures.
nist_family: CP – Contingency Planning; IR – Incident Response

description: Critical systems must be identified for recovery prioritization.
remediation: Document the most critical systems and recovery priorities.
plain_language_feedback: The organization should know which systems must come back first.
technical_feedback: Maintain a recovery priority inventory with dependencies, owners, and target recovery times.

description: Recovery evidence must be retained.
remediation: Store restore logs, screenshots, approval notes, and recovery validation records.
plain_language_feedback: Recovery actions should be documented so the organization can prove what was done.
technical_feedback: Retain restoration logs, approval evidence, recovery tickets, and validation results.
nist_family: CP – Contingency Planning; AU – Audit and Accountability

description: Tamper-evident logging must be enabled.
remediation: Enable tamper-evident logging or equivalent integrity protection for logs.
plain_language_feedback: Logs should show if someone tried to change or hide evidence.
technical_feedback: Use immutable logging, write-once controls, or validated integrity protections.

description: Unauthorized modification detection must be enabled.
remediation: Enable integrity monitoring or equivalent detection for unauthorized changes.
plain_language_feedback: The organization should be able to detect if files or records were changed improperly.
technical_feedback: Confirm file integrity monitoring, alerting, and response procedures for unexpected changes.
reference: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR 164.312(c); NIST SP 800-53 SI-7

description: Backup integrity checks must be performed.
remediation: Perform and document backup verification or integrity checks.
plain_language_feedback: Backups should be checked to make sure they are complete and trustworthy.
technical_feedback: Use checksums, backup verification jobs, and validation records.
nist_family: CP – Contingency Planning; SI – System and Information Integrity

description: Restoration testing must confirm recoverability and integrity.
remediation: Test restoration procedures and verify restored data integrity.
plain_language_feedback: Restored data should be tested to make sure it still works correctly.
technical_feedback: Validate restore procedures, application integrity, and record consistency after testing.
